# Agria (01, engineer) — SPD-043

## Brief
Close the class of command words the Bash hook reads as kind `other` because they are built from a parameter expansion it does not resolve, and of wrappers or globs reached through a variable, for a member (callers with an agent_id; Spud stays unaffected, as in SPD-044 and SPD-046).

Where: bin/spud_ledger.py. analyse_words (about line 7770) runs the prefix loop (assignments, reserved words, `-`, wrappers); the command-word dispatch follows at about line 7822, where VARREF_RE (line 5618, `$X` or `${X}` whole) resolves a known variable and the SUBST check refuses `$(...)` as kind `var`. Tests in tests/test_hooks.py beside GlobCommandWordTest (SPD-041) and GitProgramTest (SPD-046), red first.

Holes, probed by Roseval (SPD-041) with a fake VCS binary on a scratch PATH, zsh 5.9 -f and bash 3.2, each read as kind other with no finding:
- `${X:-git} push` (any operator form: `:-`, `-`, `:=`, `:+`, `#`, `%`, `/`, `^`, `,`, zsh flags such as `${(L)X}`, `${~X}`, `${=X}`)
- `X=g Y=it; $X$Y push` and `g$X push` (concatenation, partial expansion)
- `arr=(git); ${arr[1]} push` (zsh) or `${arr[0]} push` (bash)
- `X=env; $X git push` (a wrapper reached through a variable: after a bare variable resolves, the prefix loop is not run again)
- `X='g?t'; $X push` (a glob held in a variable; bash expands it). Check whether SPD-041's active_glob_word branch already closes this; if so, a test that pins it is enough.

Design, settled by Spud:
1. Fail closed. For a member, any word the dispatch reads by name (the same set SPD-041 deglobs: the command word, a wrapper's options and command, git's options and verb and the arguments git_refused reads, a shell's options, python's options and script, a spud call's arguments) that holds `$` or a backtick the hook cannot resolve to known words is refused as kind `var`, like SUBST. Resolve only what is exact: a bare `$X`/`${X}` whose value the hook knows. Do not model operator semantics; `${X:-git}` is refused, not evaluated. Mind `$'...'` (ANSI-C quoting) and `$"..."`: find out how shell_tokens reads them and refuse or read them exactly, whichever is correct in both shells. Arithmetic `$((...))` and zsh `$[...]` in a dispatched word are refused too.
2. A resolved bare variable's words go back through analyse_words in full (assignments, wrappers, `-`, globs), not only when they hold a glob, so `X=env; $X git push` reaches the git branch.
3. Do not regress what is silent today: a known bare variable naming an allowed command (`X=ls; $X`), expansions in ordinary arguments of non-dispatched commands (`echo $HOME`, `ls ${DIR:-.}`), and Spud's own calls. Where the git branch already reads `$` in an argument (git_refused, around line 7474), keep its behaviour unless a hole is shown.

Evidence first: probe from the scratchpad that both shells run what you test (a fake `git` on a scratch PATH that writes a marker file in the scratchpad; never a real write to the repository or a remote). Record in `member log` which forms you probed and in which shell.

Proof: red-first tests, then green; a differential over the pre-change hook on a broad corpus of command strings (as Atlantic did at SPD-044 and Sieglinde at SPD-046) listing every string whose verdict changed, each one intended, with zero refused-to-silent changes; the full suite passing (`python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, about six minutes, 638 tests at start). Report the new count.

Out of scope, file a proposal if you find more: zsh short loop forms (SPD-042), git aliases in on-disk config (SPD-047), file-writing git options (SPD-049), tilde or other non-parameter expansions in the command word if they turn out to hide a command.

## Ticket proposals
- **Bash hook: a trap string runs a command the hook never reads (Law 7)** — suggested P1; created as [[SPD-054]] at P1 by Spud.
  Why: trap stores shell code the shell runs later (EXIT, DEBUG before every command, ERR, signals), and analyse_words dispatches trap as kind other, so a member's git write inside a trap string is silent.
  Evidence: Probed from the SPD-043 scratchpad with a fake git first on PATH (zsh 5.9 -f, zsh -f -o nobareglobqual, bash 3.2, sh): trap 'git push' EXIT ran git push in all four; the hook on main reads kind other with no finding. SPD-043 only treats trap as leaving every variable uncertain. The harness itself refuses shell text naming trap in a worktree session, which is no cover for the hook in other sessions.
- **Bash hook: an assignment-shaped word after a wrapper is its command, which the hook skips as an assignment (Law 7)** — suggested P2; created as [[SPD-055]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: After strip_wrapper the prefix loop reads the wrapper's arguments as shell words, so NAME=value is taken for an assignment and dropped; the wrapper (nice, command, exec, nohup, timeout, xargs ...) execs that word, and a word holding a slash runs as a path.
  Evidence: Probed from the SPD-043 scratchpad (zsh 5.9 -f, zsh -f -o nobareglobqual, bash 3.2, sh) with a directory named 'x=.' holding a fake git: nice x=./git push ran git push in all four; the hook reads push as the command, kind other, no finding. env and sudo do take NAME=value as environment, so the fix is per wrapper. SPD-043 left wrapper arguments as before; only the shell's own command position stopped reading expanded words as assignments.
- **Acceptance: CutoverReadinessTest counts only the home's notes, so BadTakes tickets rendered into ledger/ fail three tests** — suggested P1; created as [[SPD-056]] at P1 by Spud.
  Why: Since BAD-001 and BAD-002 were rendered and committed into the home ledger (commits dccf137, f7a4783), the live-HEAD round trip imports 55 tickets while the test's corpus counts 53, and import events name ledger/tickets/BAD-00n.md and ledger/teams/BADS-00n/*.md that sources() leaves out. The suite is red on a clean branch from main, which blocks Spud's rerun-the-suite landing step for every ticket.
  Evidence: On the SPD-043 worktree (HEAD 51f4eba plus hook-only changes): test_acceptance.CutoverReadinessTest test_import_counts_match_the_corpus (55 != 53), test_import_events_point_at_the_source_paths (extra BAD/BADS paths) and test_every_source_file_is_generated_and_nothing_else fail; the tests exercise init, import and render, none of the Bash hook code SPD-043 changed.

## Result
SPD-043 in bin/spud_ledger.py and tests/test_hooks.py, worktree spd-043-param-expansion-command-word, uncommitted.

THE FIX. For a member, a word the Bash hook reads by name is refused when it holds an expansion the hook cannot resolve exactly. These are the words SPD-041 deglobs: the command word, a wrapper's options and command, git's options, verb and checked arguments, a shell's options, python's options and script, and a spud call's words. The expansions are operator forms such as ${X:-git}, zsh flags and modifiers (${(L)X}, $~X, $X:t), subscripts, concatenations ($X$Y, g$X, ${X}it), arithmetic, $'...' and $"...", substitutions, and unknown variables. Expansions are checked before globs. A command-word bare variable or substitution stays kind var and stops, as before. A partial expansion (${HOME}/bin/spud) is kind var but is dispatched as spelled, so Spud's checks still read it. Other words get a var-word finding. bash_reason sorts var-word and var-doubt last, so Law 7, Law 6, git-program and actor reasons survive. Spud's refusals and allows are unchanged.

A bare $X or ${X} (quoted too) is resolved only from a value the line assigned, read as bash reads it and as zsh does. Bash splits on blanks and makes glob characters active even when they were quoted in the assignment; for an array it takes the first element. Zsh takes the value as one word when it holds a blank, and every element of an array. The words go back through the whole prefix loop. X=env; $X git push and X=; $X git push reach git, and V=push; git $V reads git push. Words an expansion gives in the command position are never assignments or reserved words. Appends, values holding $ or a substitution, and an assigned IFS are unknown. neutralize_quoted_globs now marks literal dollars (single-quoted, escaped, last in double quotes), $'...' and $"...", and where $name ends at a quote or escape ($X"t").

STALE VALUES, found and probed beyond the brief. Each of these left the hook reading a value the shell no longer held, and each is now doubted: a conditional, compound, subshell, pipeline or background assignment; a function or loop body (sticky); a prefix assignment; read, printf -v, getopts, unset, mapfile and other assigning builtins; a declaration with options; a for/select header; ${X:=v}; a substitution or sh -c; trap, source and . (all). A doubted variable is still read and adds a var-doubt finding.

PROOF. Probes in zsh 5.9 -f, zsh -f -o nobareglobqual, bash 3.2 and sh, with a fake git in the scratchpad, are in the log. Red first: ParameterExpansionCommandWordTest has 11 methods; against the unchanged bin, 10 failed with 262 subtest failures. Green now. The glob-in-variable case is pinned: X='g?t' was not closed by SPD-041 (its ? reached the value quoted); X=g?t was. Two existing expectations were touched, both within this ticket: SpudAllowIdentityTest's function-shadowing python3.14 prefix is now refused for the lead (its body's "$@" is python's script), Spud silent, neither allowed; and the new class's Spud allow cases. Differential of old against new analysis over 4097 commands (every string constant in tests, .format templates expanded, probe files, generated templates with 21 expansion forms in 27 positions and 15 variable prefixes): 412 changed, zero refused-to-silent for members or Spud, each reviewed. There are 405 member silent-to-refused, 2 reason changes (Law 7 or actor to var, still refused), 2 Spud silent-to-refused (X=env; $X spud --as <member> member log, Law 5, exact), and no redirect or cd reading changed. Full suite: Ran 649 (638 + 11). The only failures are 3 CutoverReadinessTest tests unrelated to this change: HEAD holds BAD-001/002 and BADS notes, 55 tickets imported against a corpus of 53 (proposal 50). In-process analyse_command time moved from 11 to 12 us on a plain line and from 61 to 70 us on a compound line.

COSTS. A member is refused a double-quoted unknown variable at a read point: git -C "$PWD", python3 "$SCRIPT", env FOO="$BAR", member log "$M". Doubt is conservative: {X=ls;}; $X, and if X=git; then $X ... . A single-quoted $ in a spud message stays allowed.

PROPOSALS: 48 trap strings unread (P1), 49 assignment-shaped word after a wrapper is its command, nice x=./git push (P2), 50 acceptance corpus vs BadTakes notes (P1). No sub-agents. CLAUDE.md suite count becomes 649.
